source.title: Neural Redshift: Random Networks are not Random Functions
source.authors: Damien Teney; A. Nicolicioiu; Valentin Hartmann; Ehsan Abbasnejad

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether architectural inductive biases relate to generalization using complexity measures and tasks different from those in the listed versions; it does not test any version’s specific claim.
record.gate_note: Reports trained-model generalization results on modulo-arithmetic and Colored-MNIST tasks, plus reconstruction behavior on coordinate-MLPs. It also measures random-network and generated-sequence complexity, but those measures alone are not test-error results.
record.test_reason: The study tests architectural complexity biases and their association with generalization, but none of V1–V8. Its trained-model results concern activation functions, activation scaling, shortcut learning and coordinate reconstruction. Random-network complexity is not a measure of the width–test-error relationship or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute preferred function complexity to architecture, observable with random weights, and argue that alignment with target complexity can aid generalization without guaranteeing it. They explicitly retain a role for optimization and acknowledge that their complexity measures capture only part of architectural bias.
record.recipe_differences: Studies random-weight function complexity and uses small synthetic or image-representation tasks; it does not compare random-label memorization with natural-label generalization under standard training.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function, activation prefactor or weight magnitude, depth, residual connections, layer normalization, multiplicative interactions, and task complexity affect reported complexity or task performance.

fits_no_version.finding: ReLU MLPs generalize on low-frequency modulo tasks but can fit higher-frequency training data without generalizing. Gaussian activation performance depends on prefactor, with the optimum shifting upward for more complex tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice and scaling affect generalization on synthetic tasks; matching architectural complexity bias to target complexity can help but is insufficient.

fits_no_version.finding: On Colored-MNIST regression, small prefactors favor reliance on color, while digit performance peaks at an intermediate prefactor and declines beyond it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural complexity bias affects shortcut reliance and held-out regression performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Coordinate reconstructions vary with activation and initial weight magnitude. The inverse-Fourier model fits training pixels perfectly but predicts visually random values elsewhere.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and initialization magnitude affect interpolation behavior in coordinate networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-network function complexity depends on architectural components but is reported as insensitive to width; untrained transformer sequence compressibility also varies with architectural choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture shapes function and sequence complexity before training.

record.problems: Most evidence for trained-model performance is plotted without tabulated values or reported uncertainty. The tasks are synthetic, shortcut-feature, or image-representation tasks; the paper does not test natural-label classification against random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numeric test-error rows could be recovered from the supplied figures. Random-network complexity and random-transformer sequence-complexity results were not entered as rows because they do not report the generalization behavior described by the versions.

untested.parts: The paired comparison of fixed-random-label memorization, natural-label generalization and chance performance on random-label test data.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error. Width-independent complexity in random networks does not test this.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, learned sparsity and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, optimizer switching and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove those effects.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples, followed by retraining and test evaluation.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its correctly empty version links. T6/discusses applies relative to these eight versions. Row states are cannot_determine because no listed version's effect is measured; this does not negate the reported qualitative findings. No additional results bearing on V1–V8 were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold with test error is reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison is reported.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison is reported.
No large-batch versus small-batch comparison is reported.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and training-test error gaps are not measured.
No training examples are removed or retrained on.

rows.subject: ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained on modulo-arithmetic classification tasks; exact task-specific training settings not stated here.
rows.note: Text states the ReLU MLP solves only the low-frequency version; it can fit higher-frequency versions perfectly on training data but fails to generalize.
rows.check: No listed version applies. Appendix D specifies full-batch Adam, learning rate 0.001, 3,000 iterations and five seeds. The note also describes higher-frequency conditions absent from this row's condition field; those should be separate results.

rows.subject: Gaussian-activated MLPs
rows.operation_detail: Trained on modulo-arithmetic classification tasks with a multiplicative prefactor varied.

conditions.value: low-, medium-, and high-frequency modulo addition

rows.note: Text says some models with other activations generalize on all task versions when the prefactor is correctly tuned; the optimum shifts right on more complex tasks.
rows.check: No listed version applies. Split by task frequency and prefactor to represent the conditional performance. Appendix D specifies full-batch Adam, learning rate 0.001, 3,000 iterations and five seeds; Figure 7 averages seeds and Figure 8 displays individual seeds.

rows.subject: TanH-activated MLPs
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Colored-MNIST regression with a multiplicative prefactor varied.

conditions.value: digit correlated with label; color randomized

rows.note: Authors state digit accuracy is easier at an intermediate prefactor and reaches a sweet spot; exact values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: No listed version applies. This is regression performance, measured as 1−MAE, across multiple prefactors rather than one classification accuracy. Appendix D specifies full-batch Adam, learning rate 0.002 and 10,000 iterations.

rows.subject: ReLU coordinate-MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained to represent the cameraman image using a subset of pixels and evaluated on a grid.
rows.note: Authors describe learned functions as smoothing image details and favoring large uniform regions; no numeric held-out error is stated.
rows.check: No listed version applies. Figure 13 shows qualitative reconstruction on the full grid, including training pixels, rather than a separately reported held-out error. Initial weight magnitude varies and should be recorded as a condition.

rows.subject: Unbiased model
rows.operation_detail: Trained to represent the cameraman image using a subset of pixels and evaluated on a grid.
rows.measure: Training fit and predictions on other pixels
rows.value: perfect accuracy on the training data; predictions on other pixels look essentially random
rows.note: This is the specifically constructed inverse-Fourier architecture; the text states training fit and qualitative behavior away from training points.
rows.check: Perfect training fit and visually random predictions elsewhere are stated explicitly, but do not test V1: there is no natural-label versus fixed-random-label comparison. The subject is the specially constructed inverse-Fourier architecture.

rows.subject: ReLU coordinate-MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained on sparse points of the waves data and evaluated on full data.
rows.note: The text describes consistent behavior across initial weight magnitudes, but no specific test-error result.
rows.check: No listed version applies. Figure 14 gives qualitative reconstructions across initial weight magnitudes, without a numerical generalization measure. Record the varied magnitude as a condition.

rows.subject: Sine-activated coordinate-MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained on sparse points of the waves data and evaluated on full data.
rows.note: The text says sine activations can enable learning parity from sparse points, but this figure's specific reconstruction result is not described in numeric terms.
rows.check: No listed version applies. Figure 14 concerns waves reconstruction, not the separate parity claim mentioned in the note. It varies initial weight magnitude and provides no numerical reconstruction error.
